title: 4D Command IR — three-layer syntax schema
description: Layer 1: per-command signatures. Layer 2: shared substructures (enums, sub-grammars, protocols, handle types, callback contracts) referenced by pointer. Layer 3: relationships between command/overload entries.

enums.description: Layer 2 — named, reusable constant sets (e.g. Field and Variable Types). Referenced from parameters via {"kind":"enum_ref","enum":"<key>"}.

subGrammars.description: Layer 2 — 4D-native mini-grammars fully specifiable from 4D's own docs (e.g. dotted attribute paths with [] array markers). Referenced via {"kind":"subgrammar_ref","grammar":"<key>"}.

foreignGrammars.description: Layer 2 — external, non-4D grammars (SQL, regex, WSDL, JS, ...) that this corpus cannot itself fully specify. Referenced via {"kind":"foreign_grammar","grammar":"<key>"}.

protocols.description: Layer 2 — multi-statement or multi-command usage protocols that no single call's signature can express alone.

handleTypes.description: Layer 2 — opaque reference/handle types produced by some commands and consumed by others (DOM refs, SAX contexts, list refs, ...).

callbackContracts.description: Layer 2 — expected calling conventions for methods registered as callbacks (e.g. ON ERR CALL targets).

commands.description: Layer 1 — one entry per command, each with one or more overloads.

classes.description: Layer 2 — per-class metadata for the OOP corpus, keyed by ClassDef.id. Authored once and referenced from OOP member entries via CommandEntry.receiver.classId. Absent from the classic corpus.

relationships.description: Layer 3 — edges between command/overload entries: supersession, mutual exclusion, near-duplicate deltas, structural equivalence, mechanism families, platform variants.

^_.description: Underscore-prefixed root keys carry non-schema bookkeeping (e.g. '_source' provenance notes on hand-authored registry files) and are stripped by the assembler. Allowed so those files validate standalone.

CommandRef.description: Pointer to a command entry (optionally scoped to a specific overload index, 0-based) or, for OOP Layer-3 edges, to a class in root.classes. Exactly one of `command` / `classId` is used.

corpus.description: Which IR document the referenced id lives in. Omitted means the same document as the reference. Needed because the classic and OOP corpora are separate documents (out/4d-command-ir.json and out/4d-oop-ir.json) that reference each other.

rules.description: Plain-language grammar rules (e.g. dot-separates path segments; trailing [] marks an array attribute; optional letter inside [] names an element reference).

validatableByThisCorpus.description: Always false — flags that this corpus has no authority to check well-formedness of this grammar.

MultiCallChainProtocol.description: Category A — a command called repeatedly, each call contributing one unit, with a leading/trailing marker distinguishing 'more to come' from 'execute now'.

leadingDiscriminatorParam.description: Name of the optional leading param (e.g. conjOp) used to join this call to the previous one, if any.

continuationParam.description: Name of the trailing param (typically literal *) whose presence means 'more calls coming' and whose absence triggers execution.

StateMachineProtocol.description: Category L — a small grammar over a *family* of distinct named commands that must be called in a valid nested/ordered sequence (e.g. SAX open/set/close).

HandleTypeDef.description: Category M — produce/consume/destroy lifecycle for an opaque reference type.

CallbackContractDef.description: Category N — the implicit expected signature of a method registered as a callback, documented only in prose about the callback target, not in the registering command's own signature.

trigger.description: What causes 4D to invoke the registered method.

TypeRef.description: A single type reference. oneOf several kinds, covering concrete types, 4D's own catch-all pseudo-types, pointers whose target can't be resolved statically, literal-symbol sets, and pointers into the Layer 2 shared tables.

name.description: e.g. Text, Integer, Real, Boolean, Date, Time, Picture, Blob, Object, Collection, Table, Field, Array, Variable, or a 4D.<Class> OOP type.

oneOf.description: Category O — fake/catch-all types 4D uses because the real type varies by context or can't be pinned down.

possibleTargets.description: e.g. ["Table", "Field"] — what the pointer might reference; not distinguishable from the call site.

oneOf.description: Category S — statically indistinguishable overload targets.
Category D — value drawn from a shared, globally-referenced enum (e.g. Field and Variable Types constants).
Multi-type parameter, e.g. 'Text, Real, Date, Time'.

sentinelValues.description: Category H — reserved special values carved out of an otherwise-open type.

blocksOnOmission.description: Category E — omitting this parameter triggers a blocking interactive UI dialog rather than a default.

silentCoercionDefault.description: Category P — deterministic fallback conversion applied when this parameter's type can't be resolved (often across a language boundary).

elementTypeSelectsMode.description: Category G — for array-typed parameters where the element type (e.g. Integer vs Boolean) changes the whole call's semantics, not just coerces.

VariadicGroup.description: Category B — a named cluster of 1+ parameters that repeats as a unit within a single call.

ContentBindingPair.description: A matched pair: one param holds literal content, the other a live variable/pointer binding to the same content (e.g. headerName/headerVar).

OverloadElement.description: One slot in an overload's parameter list: a plain parameter, a variadic group, or a content/binding pair.

returnsNullable.description: The return value can be Null or undefined (e.g. Collection.find() with no match). Distinct from `returns: null`, which means the call returns nothing at all.

rawSyntax.description: OOP only — the source `Syntax` string this overload was parsed from, verbatim. Kept so a consumer can always see exactly what the documentation said, and so the parser's round-trip gate can be re-checked from the IR alone.

semanticRole.description: Category C (part 2) / general — short discriminator of what THIS overload does, distinct from sibling overloads even when types look similar.

mechanism.description: e.g. 'static_variadic', 'indirect_array_of_pointers', 'object_map_equivalent' — flags when two overloads solve the same problem via structurally different means (MULTI SORT ARRAY case).

discriminatedBy.description: How a caller/generator picks this overload vs siblings.

staticallyDistinguishable.description: Category S — set false when this overload cannot be told apart from a sibling by declared types alone.

jointConstraints.description: Category R — cross-parameter validation rules among named siblings, not expressible as independent per-param rules.

interactionNotes.description: Free-text notes on directional/partial overrides between named optional params (e.g. MODIFY SELECTION's two trailing *'s).

allOf.description: Every entry carries overloads except OOP properties (which carry an accessor instead) and class entries (which carry no signature at all).

kind.description: 'oop_method' is a deprecated alias retained so pre-existing consumers keep validating; new OOP entries use oop_function / oop_property / oop_constructor / oop_class.

memberName.description: OOP only — the bare member name as written at a call site, including its leading dot (e.g. '.diff', '.length'). Distinct from `id`, which is receiver-qualified.

receiver.description: OOP only — what this member is called on. Required in practice for every OOP member entry; omitted for classic commands, which have no receiver.

accessor.description: OOP properties only — read/write/computed semantics and the property's type. Properties have no `overloads`.

dynamicMember.description: OOP only — this member's name is not fixed; it stands for a user-model-derived name (e.g. Entity's .attributeName). `namePattern` describes what a real name looks like.

errorModel.description: How failure is reported. Classic commands set the OK/error system variables; OOP members typically throw or return a status object.

returnsShape.description: Structure of a returned Object, when the docs describe its members in prose (e.g. Entity.save() returning {success, status, statusText}). Optional, prose-derived, overlay-correctable.

protocolRefs.description: Category A/L — keys into root.protocols.multiCallChains / .stateMachines that this command participates in.

handleRoles.description: Category M — which handle type(s) this command produces/consumes/destroys.

callbackContractRef.description: Category N — key into root.callbackContracts, if this command registers a callback.

externalSchemaSource.description: Category K — signature/valid-values are only fully knowable from an external artifact, not this doc.

constraints.description: Prose-derived rules not expressible as types (e.g. 'must specify aTable, cannot use default table').

gatedBy.description: e.g. a compatibility setting that must be enabled for the change to apply.

docPage.description: Official documentation permalink for this command, e.g. 'https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/copy-array'. Deliberately version-less: a versioned URL stops resolving once that release is superseded, which would rot a redistributable artifact on 4D's release schedule. Null only for an entry with no documentation page.

docPageLocal.description: Path of the API page in the local docs mirror, relative to the repository root, e.g. 'mirror/docs/21-R3/API/SMTPTransporterClass.html'. This is the file the pipeline actually parsed, kept for provenance and re-derivation; consumers of the redistributable IR ship without the mirror and should use docPage instead.

Receiver.description: OOP — what an OOP member is invoked on. `instance` covers `$c.length` (a live object of the class), `class` covers `4D.File.new()` (the class object in a class store), `namespace` covers members of the class store itself (`cs.<Class>`).

inheritedFrom.description: Set when this member is declared on an ancestor class and only re-documented on `classId`'s page. Value is the declaring class's id.

Accessor.description: OOP properties — the property's type plus its read/write/computed semantics. Replaces `overloads`, which a property does not have.

oneOf.description: Two or more variants. A single-variant property uses the bare TypeRef form, so a one-element array is invalid rather than an alternative spelling.

type.description:
The property's declared type. A list when the property is multi-variant, i.e. its `Syntax` field declares several `
`-separated variants (`.bcc : Text` / `: Object` / `: Collection`). Multi-variant properties are the property-side analogue of function overloads; collapsing them to a single type silently narrows what a caller may legally assign.

computed.description: Value is derived on each read rather than stored (so reading it may have a cost or may reflect live state).

nullable.description: The property can hold Null or be undefined.

rawSyntax.description: The property's declaration line, verbatim from the documentation (e.g. `**.size** : Real`). The Overload-level `rawSyntax` covers functions and constructors; this covers properties, which have no overload, so every non-dynamic member carries a verbatim source line somewhere.

ErrorModel.description: How a call reports failure. Classic commands set the OK / error system variables; OOP members throw, populate a status object, or return Null.

statusObjectRef.description: When style is status_object and the shape is shared, the key of the CommandEntry whose returnsShape describes it.

ObjectShape.description: Structure of an object value described in prose rather than by a type name — used for returnsShape (e.g. {success, status, statusText}) and for option-object parameters.

presentWhen.description: Condition under which this member appears at all (e.g. 'only when success is False').

source.description: Where this shape was derived from — normally the doc page section, since it is prose-derived rather than declared.

ClassDef.description: Layer 2 — one built-in OOP class. `instantiation` is the field with no classic analogue and the one example synthesis depends on: it answers 'how does a caller obtain one of these?'.

docPage.description: Official documentation permalink for this class's API page, e.g. 'https://developer.4d.com/docs/API/SMTPTransporterClass'. Deliberately version-less: a versioned URL stops resolving once that release is superseded, which would rot a redistributable artifact on 4D's release schedule. Null for an abstract base documented only through its subclasses (e.g. Transporter).

docPageLocal.description: Path of the API page in the local docs mirror, relative to the repository root, e.g. 'mirror/docs/21-R3/API/SMTPTransporterClass.html'. This is the file the pipeline actually parsed, kept for provenance and re-derivation; consumers of the redistributable IR ship without the mirror and should use docPage instead.

typeName.description: The name used in a type declaration, e.g. '4D.File', 'Collection'.

instantiation.description: Ordered recipes for obtaining an instance, most idiomatic first. An empty list is only valid together with isAbstract or isStatic, and then `note` must say why.

expression.description: A 4D expression yielding an instance, using $-prefixed locals for anything it needs (e.g. '$f:=File("/PACKAGE/x.txt")').

requires.description: Preconditions the expression assumes — e.g. 'a datastore with a SynthTable dataclass', 'a running web server'.

producedBy.description: Id of the CommandEntry (classic or OOP) that produces the instance, when there is one.

isStatic.description: The class is only ever used through class-level members (never instantiated), e.g. a class store.

sharedSemantics.description: Whether instances are shared objects subject to Use/End use, and any related caveats.

members.description: Ids of the CommandEntry entries belonging to this class, including inherited ones.

isTemplate.description: The class is a template/protocol, not a fixed corpus entry — its concrete members depend on the user's data model (the ORDA generated cs.<DataClass> family). Members are described by pattern instead of enumerated.

constructor.description: Id of the CommandEntry for this class's `4D.<Class>.new()` constructor, when it has one. A convenience index — the same entry is also listed in `members`.

note.description: Free-text note about the class: why it is abstract, how its template members are derived, or the evidence its instantiation recipes were read from.
